PullRequest.Title: Fix sandbox state reconciliation when resuming Copilot sessions
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fix sandbox state reconciliation when resuming Copilot sessions:

- Restore a chat's confirmed sandbox opt-out through the runtime session command when current managed policy allows bypass. Missing confirmation does not authorize bypass, and current policy remains authoritative.
- Publish successfully applied sandbox state and reconcile a conflicting saved `off` selection for the affected chat only, without overwriting newer selections or changing sibling chats.
- Give new pending bypass requests precedence over previously confirmed state.
- Fail resume finalization and disconnect the unattached SDK session when managed policy rejects the sandbox update or the bypass command is rejected.
- Add regression coverage and update the agent-host architecture documentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resume a Copilot session whose chat has a confirmed sandbox bypass and current policy still allows bypass
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK resume/open, launch finalization, the sandbox session command, and diagnostics must complete before the resumed session wrapper is attached and usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the runtime `sandbox disable session` command to restore the confirmed bypass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command for the resumed session when effective confirmed state is off; no call per sibling chat or attachment scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same launch path applied one sandbox configuration through `session.options.update`; the PR changes the mechanism needed to restore bypass rather than adding collection-scaled work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command is awaited during launch finalization, so one runtime round trip is on the resume critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish applied sandbox state through SessionMetaChanged when state changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one metadata action for the target chat after successful application; unchanged state is suppressed, and sibling chats are not rewritten.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful launch sandbox application already published the applied state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local publication occurs before launch diagnostics finish, but payload size is small and independent of history beyond the existing sandbox-state metadata map.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One resumed session and its target chat; attachment scopes affect construction of readonly path arrays as before, while bypass restoration itself remains one runtime command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The sandbox operation is serialized by CopilotSessionSandbox._configSequencer; there is one launch finalization per resumed SDK session and no aggregate per-chat fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Confirmed state and selection are read from existing session metadata/configuration. There is no new cache; pending selections take precedence, and the applied-config cache is reset once for the newly opened runtime as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed launch call path, sequencer ownership, and tests asserting exactly one command and no sibling-chat mutation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime command latency varies by SDK/runtime, but it replaces the prior launch-time options update and does not increase effective boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the required restore adds no scaling fan-out and retains one serialized launch-time runtime operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resume or create a session when the runtime rejects sandbox configuration because of managed policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For resume, sandbox application and any disconnect after rejection are awaited before launch can fail; for create, the managed conflict is tolerated and metadata publication occurs before the session is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One update per launch application; open-time managed rejection may retain the pre-existing single reopen-without-config behavior before finalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The launch path already performed this options update and already retried open without the conflicting open-time config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on launch finalization for both create and resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect the unattached SDK session after resume finalization rejects the managed conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disconnect for the failed resumed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The finalizer already disconnected raw sessions for any thrown launch-finalization error; the PR makes this managed conflict enter that existing cleanup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before surfacing the launch failure, preventing an orphaned live runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch a SessionMetaChanged action containing one host conflict ID and message for tolerated create/background conflicts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One publication per target chat and distinct outstanding message; identical repeated conflicts are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Managed conflicts were logged only and did not publish a host-attributed error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication follows the failed SDK update. It is small synchronous host work; connected-client delivery is downstream of the existing action channel.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session launch or one background configuration attempt. The metadata action fans out through existing session subscribers, not per chat; connected client count is normally small.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each session's sandbox updates are serialized by its sequencer. Cleanup disconnect is one awaited operation for the unattached failed session; there is no burst across chats from a single launch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identical outstanding host conflicts are negatively coalesced by comparing the previous host error message. A later successful application replaces the error with confirmed state. No retry loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit result branch, message deduplication, and existing finalizer cleanup path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Subscriber transport cost depends on connected clients, but one deduplicated small action per outstanding conflict is bounded and not plausibly material relative to the failed SDK round trip.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: new conflict publication is deduplicated and bounded, while resume cleanup uses existing single-resource teardown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Background sandbox synchronization at turn start and after configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At turn start, sandbox synchronization is awaited before the agent loop starts; settings-triggered synchronization is serialized with path grants and other sandbox updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update SDK sandbox options when the serialized effective configuration differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one runtime call per distinct effective config; unchanged turn-start applications issue no RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same options update and serialized-config suppression existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A changed config blocks turn preflight; an unchanged config performs only local comparison and diagnostics/state checks as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the first managed-policy conflict to session subscribers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action for repeated identical failures until success or a different error message changes the outstanding conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repeated managed conflicts only logged and returned without metadata publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one small host action after the already-awaited failed runtime update; subsequent identical failures return before publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Turn frequency and distinct effective sandbox configurations. Cost does not scale per attachment or chat after the configuration has been built; only distinct conflict messages can create additional publications.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session Sequencer enforces one sandbox mutation at a time. Unchanged accepted configurations are skipped via the serialized _appliedConfig value.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm path compares JSON serialization to _appliedConfig and avoids the runtime update. Identical conflict messages are coalesced; successful synchronization clears the error by publishing accepted state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from `_appliedConfig`, Sequencer, and `reportChatSandboxConflict` equality guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact metadata transport latency is not measured, but added work occurs once per outstanding conflict rather than every turn for stable error text.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no repeated boundary call was added, and newly published failure metadata is coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench clients receive sandbox state metadata and show host or client-attributed failure notifications
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionMetaChanged handling runs on the client event path; notification display occurs immediately after parsing sandbox states.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse session-level and per-chat sandbox state entries and construct deduplication keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scan of the sandbox-state chat map per SessionMetaChanged envelope, as before; each unique host error is displayed once per connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The handler already parsed the session state and all chat sandbox states for every metadata envelope and deduplicated client errors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous client-side work on metadata delivery, but the PR adds only a discriminated key check to an already-existing scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Display a standard error notification for a host-attributed conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per unique error ID per connection; the LRU bounds retained keys to 100.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the requesting client received client-attributed rejection notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notification dispatch occurs in the envelope handler but is bounded to newly observed errors.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of sandbox-state chat entries in one session metadata envelope and number of connected clients. The map scan is pre-existing; added notifications scale only with unique host conflicts and connections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each live agent-host connection owns one listener and one 100-entry LRU. Connection changes dispose removed listeners; envelopes are handled serially by the event emitter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A per-connection 100-entry LRU deduplicates both host and client errors. Disconnect removes the listener and its captured cache, preventing unbounded lifetime retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from listener ownership, fixed LRU capacity, and unchanged iteration structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions with extremely many chats could make the pre-existing map scan larger, but the diff does not increase scan cardinality or metadata entry count per conflict beyond one target chat.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: dedupe memory is bounded and disposed, and the PR does not amplify the existing per-envelope state scan.

Scenarios.Scenario: Managed sandbox policy changes while a session contains multiple chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Policy publication updates metadata and reconciles each chat's saved selection synchronously before firing configuration change events.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in the session. The existing loop remains O(chats); the changed condition only determines whether confirmed sandbox metadata is retained when bypass is allowed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous policy reconciliation pass per policy change; no subprocess, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached by the changed condition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Policy and confirmed state are stored in in-memory maps/session metadata. No new cache key, retention, or invalidation behavior affecting collection size is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged loop and changed boolean condition immediately before it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large chat counts increase the pre-existing reconciliation loop cost, but this PR neither adds another pass nor expands the set iterated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: policy reconciliation complexity and expensive-boundary count are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all 14 changed files and all diff pages. The PR changes one launch-time sandbox application mechanism for confirmed resume bypass, adds deduplicated conflict metadata/notifications, and routes resume conflicts through existing single-session cleanup. No actionable performance regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
